name: Hydroquinone
summary: A melanogenesis-targeting depigmenting agent used for hyperpigmentation, especially when spot treatment is the goal.
good: Targeted treatment of stubborn hyperpigmentation under a structured plan.
bad: Long-term casual use without supervision or barrier respect.
clinicalPearls: This is a precision tool, not a forever cream.
mechanism: Reduces melanin synthesis in melanocytes, helping fade hyperpigmented lesions over time.
indications: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, melasma, and selected hyperpigmented lesions.
interactionNotes: Irritant stacking with strong acids or frequent exfoliation can worsen the result.

warnings: Irritation, rebound pigmentation if misused, and the need for time-limited use are important.

Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation left behind by resolved acne lesions — a marks treatment, not an active-acne treatment.
Moderate — typically 4–8+ weeks of consistent use for visible lightening.
Moderate; irritant dermatitis is possible, and prolonged high-concentration or unsupervised use carries a rare risk of exogenous ochronosis (paradoxical darkening).
This is the entire point of the ingredient — the strongest pigment-reducing agent on this page, reserved for marks rather than active inflammation.
Can be irritating with prolonged use — typically used in limited courses rather than indefinitely.
Night preferred, with daily sunscreen essential — sun exposure both worsens PIH and can undercut hydroquinone’s effect.
Often compounded with a retinoid and a mild corticosteroid in "triple combination" formulas for stubborn pigmentation; sunscreen is non-negotiable alongside it.
